basic_information.name: Deep Research Agents (OpenAI / Google)
basic_information.creator: OpenAI (ChatGPT Deep Research) and Google DeepMind (Gemini Deep Research). OpenAI launched first commercially; Google launched its own version independently. Both are proprietary products from the two leading frontier AI labs. Microsoft distributes OpenAI's implementation via Azure AI Foundry.
basic_information.release_date: Google Gemini Deep Research: December 11, 2024 (launched with Gemini 2.0, initially powered by Gemini 1.5 Pro). OpenAI Deep Research: February 2, 2025 (launched for Pro users at $200/month, powered by o3). OpenAI expanded to Plus users February 25, 2025, and to Free users in April 2025 via o4-mini lightweight version. OpenAI API access (o3-deep-research, o4-mini-deep-research): June 2025. Azure AI Foundry integration: July 2025 (public preview). Google upgraded to Gemini 2.5 Pro in mid-2025, then to Gemini 3 Pro in December 2025. Google opened the Deep Research Agent API via Interactions API in December 2025.
basic_information.license: Proprietary (both products). Neither OpenAI nor Google open-sources their deep research agents. Multiple open-source alternatives exist: LangChain open_deep_research, Local Deep Research (~95% SimpleQA), HuggingFace smolagents reproduction (55.15% GAIA), GPT Researcher.
basic_information.current_version: OpenAI: o3-deep-research and o4-mini-deep-research models (API), available in ChatGPT across all tiers with varying query limits (Free: 5/month lightweight, Plus/Team/Enterprise/Edu: 25/month, Pro: 250/month). Google: Gemini Deep Research powered by Gemini 3 Pro (as of December 2025), available via Gemini Advanced ($20/month) and via the Interactions API (beta) for developers.

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: single_agent — Both OpenAI and Google Deep Research operate as single autonomous agents that execute a long-running Plan-Act-Observe loop. They are not multi-agent systems; a single agent instance plans research queries, searches the web, reads results, identifies knowledge gaps, formulates new queries, and iterates until ready to synthesize a final report. OpenAI describes this as end-to-end reinforcement learning on browsing and reasoning tasks. Google describes it as an agentic workflow: 'a single request triggers an autonomous loop of planning, searching, reading, and reasoning.'
technical_architecture.underlying_models: OpenAI: Powered by a specialized version of the o3 model (o3-deep-research), optimized for extended web browsing and reasoning. A lightweight alternative uses o4-mini (o4-mini-deep-research), 5x cheaper with slightly less exhaustive results. The Azure AI Foundry integration adds a GPT-4-series model for clarifying intent before the research phase. Google: Initially Gemini 1.5 Pro (December 2024), upgraded to Gemini 2.5 Pro (mid-2025), then Gemini 3 Pro (December 2025). Each model upgrade significantly improved benchmark scores. Google's implementation leverages Gemini 3 Pro's visual reasoning and multimodal capabilities.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: OpenAI: Uses web search (Bing-based), file search with vector stores, and remote MCP server connectors. MCP integration requires servers implementing search and fetch tools. Pre-built OpenAI Connectors wrap popular services: Google Drive, SharePoint, Dropbox, Box, Outlook, Gmail, Google Calendar, Linear, GitHub, HubSpot, Teams. API access via Responses API. Google: Uses google_search and url_context tools by default. Can access user's Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Chat data. API access via the Interactions API (beta). Outputs can be exported to Google Docs. Both platforms support code execution for data analysis within research workflows.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: Both follow iterative planning with autonomous re-planning. OpenAI: Classic Plan-Act-Observe loop — the agent plans what to search, acts by issuing search queries, observes results by reading returned pages, then repeats. Trained via end-to-end reinforcement learning on hard browsing and reasoning tasks. The agent learned to 'plan and execute a multi-step trajectory, backtracking and reacting to real-time information.' Google: Follows a structured research plan that users can review and optionally modify before execution. The agent 'formulates queries, reads results, identifies knowledge gaps, and searches again.' Google gives the user more upfront control over the plan, while OpenAI adjusts its research path more dynamically in real-time.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: Neither product uses multi-agent architectures. Both are single-agent systems executing a research workflow autonomously. However, in the API, developers can compose deep research as one step in a larger multi-agent pipeline. Azure AI Foundry explicitly supports this: 'one agent performs deep web analysis, another generates a slide deck, while a third emails the result.' Google's ADK (Agent Development Kit) similarly allows composing deep research tasks with other agents.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: short_term (conversation context and research session state) | semantic (web-retrieved knowledge synthesized during research). Neither product has persistent episodic memory across sessions or procedural memory that learns skills over time. Each deep research task is independent — the agent does not learn from previous research sessions. Within a session, the agent maintains state across dozens or hundreds of web pages visited, accumulating findings iteratively.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: Both systems rely on long-context models to manage large amounts of retrieved information. OpenAI's o3-deep-research is optimized for long-context reasoning over extended sessions (5-30 minutes). Google's Gemini 3 Pro provides an extremely large context window (up to 1M tokens). Both systems iteratively accumulate findings during the research process, with the model progressively synthesizing information rather than holding all raw content simultaneously. The agent reads, summarizes, identifies gaps, and searches again — an implicit form of progressive summarization.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: cloud — Research results persist as generated reports (text output). OpenAI: Reports delivered in ChatGPT interface or via API response; can include structured citations. Google: Reports can be exported to Google Docs. Neither system persists the intermediate research state (search queries, visited pages, reasoning traces) for user access after completion, though OpenAI's API provides some tracing metadata. Azure AI Foundry adds enterprise audit trails.
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Context is a central architectural concern for both products. The entire deep research paradigm is essentially a context engineering exercise: the agent must decide what information to gather, when it has enough, and how to synthesize it coherently. OpenAI's approach uses reinforcement learning to train the agent to manage its own context — learning when to backtrack, when to search deeper, when to pivot. Google's approach provides the user visibility into the research plan, allowing human input on context priorities before execution. Both systems treat the web itself as an extended knowledge base, with the agent performing retrieval-augmented generation at scale.

capabilities.core_capabilities: Both products share a core capability: autonomous long-running web research that produces comprehensive, cited reports. Specific capabilities include: (1) Multi-step web search — autonomously issuing dozens to hundreds of search queries, reading full web pages, PDFs, and images, (2) Knowledge gap identification — recognizing when information is incomplete and formulating follow-up queries, (3) Cross-source synthesis — combining information from multiple sources into a coherent narrative, (4) Citation generation — producing reports with inline citations linked to source URLs, (5) Multi-modal analysis — OpenAI can interpret text, images, and PDFs; Google Gemini 3 Pro adds visual reasoning with charts and data visualization in reports, (6) Data analysis — both can execute code for quantitative analysis within research workflows, (7) Structured output — producing organized reports with sections, tables, and formatted data. OpenAI-specific: MCP connector integration allows research across internal company data (Google Drive, SharePoint, Dropbox, GitHub, etc.); Azure AI Foundry integration for enterprise workflows; o4-mini lightweight mode for cost-efficient research. Google-specific: Integration with Gmail, Drive, and Chat for personal data research; export to Google Docs; visual reports with animations for Ultra users; API via Interactions API. Performance benchmarks: OpenAI o3-deep-research scored 26.6% on Humanity's Last Exam (vs 3.3% GPT-4o), ~72-73% on GAIA (vs ~63-67% prior best), 58% on GAIA Level 3 (vs <50% prior). Google Gemini Deep Research (Gemini 3 Pro) scored 46.4% on HLE (vs 43.2% Gemini 3 Pro base), 66.1% on DeepSearchQA, 59.2% on BrowseComp.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Text, web browsing, PDF analysis, image interpretation (OpenAI), code execution, data analysis. OpenAI deep research can interpret images and PDFs found on the web. Google Gemini Deep Research initially was text-only but Gemini 3 Pro upgrade added visual reasoning. Both produce text-based reports; Google adds visual elements for Ultra users.
capabilities.autonomy_level: fully_autonomous — Both products operate independently after receiving a prompt. The user submits a research question and receives a completed report 5-60 minutes later with no intermediate human intervention required. Google offers an optional step where users can review and modify the research plan before execution begins, but execution itself is autonomous. Neither product requires approval during the research process.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: OpenAI: Web search (Bing-based), file search with vector stores, MCP server connectors, OpenAI Connectors for popular services (Google Drive, SharePoint, Dropbox, Box, Gmail, Outlook, GitHub, HubSpot, Linear, Google Calendar, Teams). Google: google_search, url_context, Gmail integration, Google Drive integration, Google Chat integration, Google Docs export. Both: code execution/data analysis capabilities within research workflows.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: OpenAI: Full MCP support for deep research. The o3-deep-research and o4-mini-deep-research models accept remote MCP servers as data sources. MCP servers must implement search and fetch tools. OpenAI also provides pre-built Connectors (MCP wrappers) for popular services. Approval mode must be set to 'never' since operations are read-only. Google: No explicit MCP support for Gemini Deep Research. Google has its own tool integration approach via the Interactions API and ADK (Agent Development Kit). [uncertain for Google MCP]
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: Neither OpenAI nor Google Deep Research explicitly implements the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol as of February 2026. However, both can be composed as steps in multi-agent pipelines via their respective APIs. Google's ADK supports multi-agent orchestration separately. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: No — Deep Research agents operate on web content and user-provided data, not on code repositories. AGENTS.md is relevant to coding agents (Devin, Claude Code, Cursor) rather than research agents. Neither product reads or respects AGENTS.md files.
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: OpenAI: Strong API-level compatibility. The Responses API and MCP support allow integration with any framework that can make HTTP calls. Azure AI Foundry provides enterprise-grade orchestration with other Azure services and agents. Can be composed with LangChain, AutoGen, and other frameworks via API. Google: The Interactions API (beta) provides programmatic access. Can be integrated with Google's ADK for multi-agent workflows. Python SDK support via google-genai library. Less ecosystem breadth than OpenAI's approach given the newer API.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: Both products operate in a read-only sandbox for web content. OpenAI: Deep research agents browse the web and read documents but cannot modify external systems. MCP approval mode is set to 'never' (read-only). File search operates on user-uploaded vector stores. Azure AI Foundry adds enterprise security controls, compliance, and data governance. Google: Research is read-only web browsing. Gmail/Drive access requires user opt-in. Google's enterprise deployment (Gemini Enterprise) adds organizational data governance.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Neither product has mid-research escalation — both operate fully autonomously during the research phase. Google's pre-execution plan review is the closest to escalation: users can modify the research plan before the agent begins. OpenAI provides no plan review step — the agent begins researching immediately. Post-research, both deliver reports for human review. In enterprise contexts (Azure AI Foundry, Gemini Enterprise), organizations can implement approval workflows around the research outputs.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Both products use citations as their primary hallucination mitigation strategy, linking claims to source URLs. OpenAI: Trained via reinforcement learning specifically on browsing and reasoning tasks to improve factual accuracy. The o3 model includes chain-of-thought reasoning that can be audited. However, known issues exist — citation accuracy is imperfect, with some reports containing hallucinated or incorrect references. Scored 26.6% on Humanity's Last Exam (meaning 73.4% of expert-level questions were answered incorrectly or not answered). Google: Gemini Deep Research is 'specifically trained to reduce hallucinations and maximize report quality.' The December 2025 upgrade improved accuracy on multiple benchmarks. Google's structured plan approach allows users to verify the research direction before execution. Both: Users must independently verify critical claims — neither product guarantees citation accuracy.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: OpenAI: The API provides reasoning traces and metadata about the research process. Azure AI Foundry adds full audit trails with 'citations, internal prompts, and a reasoning trail that is fully auditable.' ChatGPT consumer interface shows browsing activity during research. Google: The Gemini interface shows research progress and sources consulted. The Interactions API provides intermediate states and tool call logs. Google Docs export preserves the report with citations for record-keeping.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: post_review — Both products generate complete reports autonomously, then present them for human review. Google adds an optional pre-approval step for the research plan. Neither product pauses mid-research for human input. The pattern is: prompt → (optional plan review for Google) → autonomous research → completed report → human review. Enterprise deployments can add post-review approval workflows before reports are acted upon.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: None — Both are proprietary products not governed by external standards bodies. OpenAI and Google each set their own safety and quality standards. Microsoft's Azure AI Foundry distribution adds Microsoft's Responsible AI framework. Google applies its own AI Principles. Neither product is governed by AAIF, Linux Foundation, or ISO standards specifically.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: OpenAI: Implements MCP (Model Context Protocol) for tool integration, originally created by Anthropic and now widely adopted. Uses the Responses API as its interface standard. Azure distribution follows Azure AI Foundry conventions. Google: Created the Interactions API as a new standard for agentic model interactions. Gemini Deep Research is the flagship application of this API. Google also created the ADK (Agent Development Kit) and A2A protocol, though Deep Research itself does not explicitly implement A2A.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: OpenAI: SOC 2 certified (OpenAI platform). Azure AI Foundry deployment adds enterprise compliance: SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR. OpenAI's platform is subject to EU AI Act requirements as a general-purpose AI system. Google: Google Cloud / Gemini Enterprise includes SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR compliance. Both companies are classified as providers of general-purpose AI models under the EU AI Act and must comply with transparency and documentation requirements. Specific deep research feature compliance certifications beyond platform-level are not separately documented. [uncertain]

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: cloud | managed_service — Both products are cloud-only. OpenAI: Available via ChatGPT (consumer/business), OpenAI API, and Azure AI Foundry (enterprise managed service). No local or edge deployment. Google: Available via Gemini app (consumer), Gemini Enterprise (Google Workspace), and Gemini API via Interactions API. No local or edge deployment. Neither product can be self-hosted or run on-premise.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: serverless — Both operate as serverless API calls from the user's perspective. OpenAI: Each deep research task runs as an independent process; multiple can run in parallel via API. Azure AI Foundry supports orchestration at enterprise scale. Google: API supports background tasks (background=True required), with concurrent request limits determined by quota tier. Both scale horizontally via their respective cloud infrastructures.
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: OpenAI o3-deep-research: $10/M input tokens, $40/M output tokens. In practice, ~$10-30 per research query via API (average ~$10/query, complex queries up to $30). o4-mini-deep-research: $2/M input tokens, $8/M output tokens — approximately 5-10x cheaper, averaging ~$1-3 per query. ChatGPT subscription includes deep research queries: Free (5 lightweight/month), Plus ($20/month, 25 queries), Pro ($200/month, 250 queries). Azure AI Foundry: same API pricing plus Bing grounding and GPT-4 clarification charges. Google: Consumer access via Gemini Advanced ($20/month) with limited monthly queries. API pricing: ~$2/M input tokens (Gemini 3 Pro pricing). Significantly cheaper per query than OpenAI's o3 model via API, though exact per-query costs depend on research complexity and token consumption.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: No local hardware requirements — all computation runs in OpenAI's or Google's cloud infrastructure. Users need only a web browser or API access. Enterprise deployments (Azure AI Foundry, Gemini Enterprise) may require organizational cloud accounts and configuration. API usage requires API keys and billing accounts.

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: OpenAI: The API returns reasoning traces and intermediate states. Azure AI Foundry provides enterprise monitoring, logging, and integration with Azure Monitor. No documented integration with third-party LLM observability tools (LangSmith, Langfuse) specifically for deep research, though the Responses API output can be logged. Google: The Interactions API provides intermediate interaction states and tool call logs. Google Cloud monitoring for Gemini Enterprise deployments. No specific third-party observability integrations documented for the deep research feature. [uncertain]
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Yes (both) — OpenAI: The API provides reasoning chains, search queries, and source URLs as part of the response. Azure AI Foundry adds 'citations, internal prompts, and a reasoning trail that is fully auditable.' Google: The Interactions API returns intermediate states including tool calls (search queries) and their results during the research process. Both platforms allow developers to trace the research process after completion.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: production_ready — Both products are deployed to millions of users in production. OpenAI Deep Research has been live since February 2025 across all ChatGPT tiers and is available via production API. Azure AI Foundry integration is in public preview (July 2025). Google Deep Research has been live since December 2024 for Gemini Advanced users. The Interactions API is in public beta (December 2025). Enterprise deployments are active at both companies. Note: while the consumer products are production-ready, the developer APIs are still in preview/beta status.

adoption_and_market.github_stars: N/A — Both are proprietary products, not open-source. Notable open-source alternatives: langchain-ai/open_deep_research (LangChain's reproduction), LearningCircuit/local-deep-research (~95% SimpleQA), btahir/open-deep-research, nickscamara/open-deep-research (Firecrawl-based), HuggingFace smolagents deep research (55.15% GAIA). Exact star counts vary but the local-deep-research project is one of the most popular.
adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: OpenAI: Deep Research is available to all 300M+ weekly ChatGPT users (Free tier gets 5 queries/month). Pro users ($200/month) have been the primary power users since launch. As of February 2026, it has been described as having 'redefined knowledge work in its first year.' Enterprise adoption via Azure AI Foundry (public preview July 2025). Google: Gemini Advanced has tens of millions of subscribers globally. Deep Research available in 100+ countries and 45+ languages since December 2024. Developer API access opened December 2025. Both: Deep research as a category has become standard — Perplexity, Grok, and other competitors have launched similar features, validating the product category.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: Freemium (both). OpenAI: Free tier (5 lightweight queries/month), Plus ($20/month, 25 queries), Pro ($200/month, 250 queries), Enterprise (custom). API: pay-per-token ($10-40/M tokens for o3, $2-8/M for o4-mini). Google: Included with Gemini Advanced ($20/month via Google One AI Premium Plan), limited monthly queries. API: pay-per-token (~$2/M input tokens). Google's consumer offering is significantly cheaper than OpenAI's full-model deep research ($20 vs $200/month for the best experience).
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: Primary use cases span knowledge work: (1) Market research and competitive intelligence — synthesizing industry trends, company data, market sizing, (2) Financial analysis — analyzing company reports, earnings data, market trends, (3) Legal research — case law review, regulatory analysis (CoCounsel launching deep research workflows in 2026), (4) Academic and scientific research — literature reviews, cross-referencing studies, (5) Policy analysis — regulatory landscape mapping, compliance research, (6) Due diligence — investment research, company background checks, (7) Technical research — architecture decisions, technology comparisons, library evaluations, (8) Journalism and content creation — fact-checking, source gathering, investigative research. Industries: Finance, law, consulting, technology, academia, media, policy/government.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: OpenAI and Google are the two market leaders in deep research agents, with fundamentally different approaches. OpenAI pioneered the category commercially and leads on precision, multimodal analysis, and enterprise integration (Azure). Google competes on price ($20 vs $200/month for best experience), speed, integration with Google ecosystem (Docs, Drive, Gmail), and has improved dramatically with Gemini 3 Pro (now outscoring OpenAI on HLE: 46.4% vs 26.6%). Key competitors: Perplexity Deep Research (fastest, 21.1% HLE, $20/month), Grok Deep Search (xAI, 10x faster than ChatGPT, integrated with X/Twitter data), Claude (Anthropic, strong reasoning but no branded 'deep research' product). Open-source alternatives are catching up: HuggingFace's smolagents reproduction scored 55.15% on GAIA. The market is rapidly commoditizing as all major AI labs add similar capabilities.

ecosystem_maturity.community_size: Both products benefit from massive existing user communities rather than dedicated deep research communities. OpenAI: 300M+ weekly ChatGPT users, active developer community on community.openai.com, extensive discussions on Reddit r/ChatGPT and r/OpenAI. Google: Tens of millions of Gemini users, developer community at discuss.ai.google.dev, active discussions on Reddit r/Bard and r/GoogleGeminiAI. Open-source deep research community is growing: multiple GitHub projects, active discussions on Hacker News, dedicated subreddits for AI research tools.
ecosystem_maturity.documentation_quality: good (both). OpenAI: Official documentation at platform.openai.com/docs/guides/deep-research covers API usage, model selection, MCP integration, and data sources. Azure AI Foundry adds enterprise documentation. Blog posts explain architecture and training approach. Google: Documentation at ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deep-research covers Interactions API, agent capabilities, and limitations. Google blog posts explain the technology. Both lack deep technical papers on the architecture — the training methodology and internal workings remain proprietary.
ecosystem_maturity.third_party_integrations_count: OpenAI: 12+ pre-built Connectors (Google Drive, SharePoint, Dropbox, Box, Gmail, Outlook, GitHub, HubSpot, Linear, Google Calendar, Teams, and more), plus unlimited custom MCP server integrations. Google: Gmail, Google Drive, Google Chat, Google Docs export — primarily Google ecosystem integrations. API allows custom tool integration but with fewer pre-built connectors than OpenAI.
ecosystem_maturity.tutorial_availability: Extensive for both. OpenAI: Official documentation, OpenAI Cookbook examples, numerous third-party tutorials on Medium, Dev.to, YouTube. IBM, Data Science Dojo, and many tech publications have published guides. Google: Official getting-started guides, Google AI blog posts, developer tutorials (e.g., philschmid.de guide), conference presentations. Both benefit from massive media coverage that serves as informal tutorials. No official certification programs for either.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: fully_delegated — Both products operate with minimal human involvement. The user provides a prompt and receives a completed report. Google adds an optional plan review step (making it closer to 'autonomous' than 'fully_delegated' when plan review is used). OpenAI provides no intermediate checkpoints — the agent runs to completion independently. In enterprise settings, organizations may add post-research review workflows, but the agent itself operates without human supervision.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Both products have a simple handoff: the agent delivers a completed report and the human takes over for review, verification, and action. OpenAI: Report delivered in ChatGPT interface or via API response with citations. Users can ask follow-up questions to refine or extend research. Google: Report delivered in Gemini interface with option to export to Google Docs. Users can view research methodology section explaining the agent's process. Neither product has mid-research handoff — you cannot intervene during the research process to redirect the agent (except by canceling and starting over).
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Limited explicit feedback loops in both products. OpenAI: Users can provide follow-up prompts to refine research, but there is no persistent learning across sessions. The underlying models are improved via OpenAI's general training pipeline (RLHF, preference data), not from individual deep research session feedback. Google: Similar — no per-user learning. Model improvements come from Google's general training pipeline. Neither product adapts to individual user preferences or research styles over time. The main feedback mechanism is iterative: users who find reports insufficient can submit refined prompts for new research sessions.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: High relevance for startup founders across multiple dimensions: (1) MARKET RESEARCH: Both tools can produce comprehensive market analysis reports in 10-30 minutes that would take a human analyst hours or days. Startups can use deep research for competitive analysis, market sizing, customer discovery, and trend analysis at a fraction of the cost of hiring consultants. (2) DUE DILIGENCE: Investors and founders can research potential partners, customers, or acquisition targets quickly. (3) TECHNICAL EVALUATION: CTOs can research technology stacks, frameworks, and architectural approaches before making build-vs-buy decisions. (4) WHEN TO USE: Best for broad, multi-source research tasks where comprehensiveness matters more than real-time accuracy — market landscapes, industry reports, literature reviews, regulatory analysis. (5) WHEN TO AVOID: Not suitable for tasks requiring real-time data (stock prices, live metrics), proprietary/internal data analysis (unless connected via MCP/Drive), or decisions where citation accuracy is critical without human verification. Deep research agents can hallucinate citations. (6) COST CONSIDERATION: Google at $20/month is extremely cost-effective for startups. OpenAI at $20/month (Plus, 25 queries) is also accessible. API costs can add up: $10-30/query for o3, $1-3/query for o4-mini. For a startup doing 50 research queries/month, expect $50-150/month via API. (7) COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE: The existence of deep research agents means your competitors have them too — the competitive advantage shifts from having access to research to asking better questions and acting faster on insights.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: BUY for general research needs. Both OpenAI and Google offer production-ready deep research at $20/month (consumer) or pay-per-query via API. Building a custom deep research agent is only justified if: (1) You need research over proprietary internal data not accessible via MCP/Connectors, (2) You need domain-specific research methodology (e.g., patent analysis, clinical trial review) beyond what generic agents provide, (3) Your core product IS a research tool competing in this space. Open-source alternatives (LangChain open_deep_research, Local Deep Research) offer customization at lower ongoing cost but require engineering investment. For most startups: use Google Gemini Deep Research at $20/month for quick research, OpenAI for deeper analysis when needed, and API access for automation. Total cost: $40-200/month for comprehensive research capabilities — far cheaper than a junior research analyst.

confidence.data_quality: High — Information sourced from official OpenAI and Google announcements, product documentation (platform.openai.com, ai.google.dev), Microsoft Azure blog, TechCrunch, Fortune, IBM Think, Nature, multiple independent benchmark evaluations, and industry analyst reports. Pricing data confirmed from official pricing pages.
confidence.cross_reference: Key data points confirmed across multiple sources: (1) OpenAI Deep Research launch date February 2, 2025 — OpenAI blog, TechCrunch, Wikipedia, (2) Google Deep Research launch December 11, 2024 — Google blog, TechCrunch, (3) HLE benchmark scores — OpenAI blog, Fortune, Scale AI leaderboard, Google blog, (4) API pricing — official pricing pages, Artificial Analysis, Medium, (5) Azure AI Foundry integration — Microsoft Azure blog, Visual Studio Magazine, InfoWorld, (6) Gemini 3 Pro upgrade December 2025 — Google blog, 9to5Google, SiliconANGLE, (7) Query limits and tier structure — OpenAI help center, multiple tech publications.
confidence.caveats: Key caveats: (1) RAPIDLY EVOLVING — Both products receive frequent updates; pricing, query limits, model versions, and capabilities change regularly. This data reflects status as of February 2026. (2) BENCHMARK SCORES vary by evaluation methodology — HLE scores are not directly comparable across products when evaluated at different times with different model versions. Google's 46.4% HLE was achieved with Gemini 3 Pro (December 2025) vs OpenAI's 26.6% with o3 (February 2025). (3) CITATION ACCURACY is imperfect for both products — hallucinated references are documented. Never use deep research output for critical decisions without independent verification. (4) API STATUS — OpenAI's deep research API is production but relatively new (June 2025). Google's Interactions API is in public beta (December 2025) and subject to breaking changes. (5) COST VOLATILITY — API costs can be unpredictable due to variable token consumption per query. A single o3 deep research query can cost $2-30+ depending on complexity. (6) COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE is rapidly commoditizing — Perplexity, Grok, and open-source alternatives are closing the gap quickly. (7) EU AI ACT implications — as general-purpose AI systems, both face evolving regulatory requirements in the European market.
